New Mexico.ag_notification_note: The Attorney General must be notified only if more than 1,000 New Mexico residents must be notified from a single breach, within the same 45 days. Smaller breaches do not trigger AG notice.
New Mexico.agency_name: New Mexico Office of the Attorney General
New Mexico.freeze_rights_note: You can place a free security freeze on your credit file with each of the three major credit bureaus, Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze blocks new accounts from being opened in your name until you lift it, and it is free to place, lift and remove under federal law.
New Mexico.notification_deadline_note: Notice must be given in the most expedient time possible, but no later than 45 calendar days after discovery of the breach. The clock can be paused for a law enforcement request or while the company determines the scope of the breach and restores its system.
New Mexico.private_right_note: There is no private right of action under the Data Breach Notification Act. Only the Attorney General may enforce it and seek civil penalties.
New Mexico.state_note: New Mexico's law does not apply to the state government or its political subdivisions, and notice is only required for unencrypted personal identifying information reasonably believed to have been subject to a breach.

New York.ag_notification_note: The company must notify the Attorney General, the Department of State and the State Police whenever any New York residents are notified, with no minimum number of people affected. Credit reporting agencies must also be told if more than 5,000 residents are notified at one time.
New York.agency_name: New York State Office of the Attorney General
New York.freeze_rights_note: You can place a free security freeze on your credit file with each of the three major credit bureaus, Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze blocks new accounts from being opened in your name until you lift it, and it is free to place, lift and remove under federal law.
New York.notification_deadline_note: Since the December 2024 amendment, notice must be given in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay, and in no event later than 30 days after discovery. The old flexibility to delay while investigating the scope of the breach was removed; only a legitimate law enforcement need can delay notice.
New York.private_right_note: There is no private right of action under the breach notification law or the SHIELD Act. Only the Attorney General may enforce them, although a court in an AG action may award an affected person actual costs or losses.
New York.state_note: New York is unusually broad: mere unauthorized access, not just actual acquisition, can trigger notice, and private information now includes biometric data, online account credentials, and medical and health insurance information. The SHIELD Act also requires businesses to maintain reasonable safeguards, not just to give notice after a breach.
New York.statute_name: SHIELD Act (Stop Hacks and Improve Electronic Data Security Act)

North Carolina.ag_notification_note: Whenever a business notifies any affected person, it must also notify the Consumer Protection Division of the Attorney General's Office without unreasonable delay, describing the breach, the number affected and the steps taken. If more than 1,000 people are notified at one time, the credit reporting agencies must also be told.
North Carolina.agency_name: North Carolina Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
North Carolina.freeze_rights_note: You can place a free security freeze on your credit file with each of the three major credit bureaus, Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze blocks new accounts from being opened in your name until you lift it, and it is free to place, lift and remove under federal law.
North Carolina.notification_deadline_note: The statute sets no fixed number of days. Notice must be given without unreasonable delay after discovery, allowing time to find contact information, determine the scope of the breach and restore the system, and a law enforcement request can delay it.
North Carolina.private_right_note: A violation is a violation of the unfair and deceptive trade practices law, but no private suit may be brought unless the individual was injured as a result of the violation.
North Carolina.state_note: North Carolina is one of the few states that requires AG notice for any breach, not just a large one, and the breach notice you receive must itself list contact information for the Federal Trade Commission and the Attorney General's Office.

North Dakota.ag_notification_note: The Attorney General must be notified by mail or email only if a breach exceeds 250 individuals. Smaller breaches do not trigger AG notice.
North Dakota.agency_name: North Dakota Office of Attorney General
North Dakota.freeze_rights_note: You can place a free security freeze on your credit file with each of the three major credit bureaus, Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze blocks new accounts from being opened in your name until you lift it, and it is free to place, lift and remove under federal law.
North Dakota.notification_deadline_note: The statute sets no fixed number of days. Notice must be given in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay, allowing time for law enforcement needs and for steps to determine the scope of the breach and restore the system.
North Dakota.private_right_note: The breach notification law provides no private right of action. Enforcement is by the Attorney General under the state's unlawful practices law.
North Dakota.state_note: North Dakota's AG threshold is low at 250 people, so many mid-size breaches still reach the Attorney General, and a person who only stores data it does not own must tell the data owner immediately after discovery.
North Dakota.statute_name: Notice of Security Breach for Personal Information

Ohio.ag_notification_note: The statute does not require notice to the Attorney General. It does require notice to the nationwide consumer reporting agencies, without unreasonable delay, if more than 1,000 Ohio residents are notified in a single occurrence.
Ohio.freeze_rights_note: You can place a free security freeze on your credit file with each of the three major credit bureaus, Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze blocks new accounts from being opened in your name until you lift it, and it is free to place, lift and remove under federal law.
Ohio.notification_deadline_note: Notice must be given in the most expedient time possible, but no later than 45 days after discovery or notification of the breach. Notice is only required when the access and acquisition causes, or reasonably is believed will cause, a material risk of identity theft or other fraud.
Ohio.private_right_note: There is no private right of action under the breach notification statute. The Attorney General may investigate and bring a civil action for a failure to comply.
Ohio.state_note: Ohio is unusual in having no AG-notice duty at all under this statute, so if you were affected, your complaint route is the Attorney General's consumer protection office even though the company was not required to tell that office about the breach.

Oklahoma.ag_notification_note: Since January 1, 2026, if 500 or more Oklahoma residents are notified from a single breach, the company must also notify the Attorney General without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after notifying the affected residents. Breaches affecting fewer than 500 residents do not trigger AG notice.
Oklahoma.agency_name: Oklahoma Office of the Attorney General
Oklahoma.freeze_rights_note: You can place a free security freeze on your credit file with each of the three major credit bureaus, Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze blocks new accounts from being opened in your name until you lift it, and it is free to place, lift and remove under federal law.
Oklahoma.notification_deadline_note: The statute sets no fixed number of days for telling affected residents. Notice must be given without unreasonable delay, allowing time to determine the scope of the breach and restore the system, and a law enforcement request can delay it.
Oklahoma.private_right_note: The breach notification statute provides no private right of action. A violation that results in injury or loss may be enforced by the Attorney General or a district attorney as an unlawful practice under the Oklahoma Consumer Protection Act.
Oklahoma.state_note: Oklahoma's AG-notice duty is new, effective January 1, 2026, and it runs on a different clock from consumer notice: up to 60 days after residents are told. The 2026 amendments also broadened covered data to include biometric data and unique electronic identifiers.

Oregon.ag_notification_note: The Attorney General must be notified, in writing or electronically, if more than 250 consumers must be notified, and must receive a copy of any consumer notice within a reasonable time if the breach affects more than 250 consumers.
Oregon.freeze_rights_note: You can place a free security freeze on your credit file with each of the three major credit bureaus, Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze blocks new accounts from being opened in your name until you lift it, and it is free to place, lift and remove under federal law. Oregon's breach notice must itself tell you about the credit bureaus and advise you to report suspected identity theft to law enforcement, the Attorney General and the Federal Trade Commission.
Oregon.notification_deadline_note: Notice must be given in the most expeditious manner possible, without unreasonable delay, but no later than 45 days after discovering or receiving notification of the breach. A vendor must tell the company it serves within 10 days, and notice can be delayed only on a written law enforcement request.
Oregon.private_right_note: A violation is an unlawful practice under the state's unlawful trade practices law, enforced by the Attorney General. The breach notification law itself gives consumers no private right of action, although the statute says other rights and remedies under law are preserved.
Oregon.state_note: Oregon requires no consumer notice at all if, after investigation or consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines consumers are unlikely to suffer harm, but it must document that determination in writing and keep it for at least five years.

Pennsylvania.ag_notification_note: The Office of Attorney General must be notified concurrently with affected residents if more than 500 Pennsylvania residents must be notified. State agencies must also notify the Attorney General concurrently, even for smaller breaches.
Pennsylvania.freeze_rights_note: You can place a free security freeze on your credit file with each of the three major credit bureaus, Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze blocks new accounts from being opened in your name until you lift it, and it is free to place, lift and remove under federal law.
Pennsylvania.notification_deadline_note: For a private company, the statute sets no fixed number of days: notice must be given without unreasonable delay after the breach is determined, allowing time to determine the scope and restore the system. State agencies, counties, public schools and municipalities have a tighter 7-business-day deadline.
Pennsylvania.private_right_note: The breach notification act itself creates no private right of action. Violations are treated as unfair or deceptive acts enforced by the Attorney General, although consumers may still pursue other theories such as negligence or consumer protection claims.
Pennsylvania.state_note: Pennsylvania is one of the few states in this set that requires free credit monitoring: when a breach exposes a Social Security, driver's license, state ID or bank account number, the company must pay for one independent credit report and 12 months of credit monitoring for affected people.
Pennsylvania.statute_name: Breach of Personal Information Notification Act

Rhode Island.ag_notification_note: The Attorney General and the major credit reporting agencies must be notified if more than 500 Rhode Island residents are to be notified, without delaying notice to the affected residents themselves.
Rhode Island.agency_name: Rhode Island Office of the Attorney General
Rhode Island.freeze_rights_note: You can place a free security freeze on your credit file with each of the three major credit bureaus, Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze blocks new accounts from being opened in your name until you lift it, and it is free to place, lift and remove under federal law. Rhode Island's breach notice must itself explain how to request a security freeze.
Rhode Island.notification_deadline_note: For a private company, notice must be given in the most expedient time possible, but no later than 45 calendar days after confirmation of the breach and being able to ascertain the information the notice must contain. State and municipal agencies have 30 calendar days. Notice is only required for a breach that poses a significant risk of identity theft.
Rhode Island.private_right_note: The Identity Theft Protection Act provides no express private right of action for consumers. A failure to notify is a violation enforced under the act's penalty provisions.
Rhode Island.state_note: Rhode Island's clock starts at confirmation of the breach, not discovery, and state and municipal agencies must provide remediation services, including at least five years of coverage for adults, while a private company's notice must describe any remediation services it is offering.

South Carolina.ag_notification_note: Notice goes to the Consumer Protection Division of the Department of Consumer Affairs, not the Attorney General, and only if more than 1,000 South Carolina residents are notified at one time. The nationwide credit reporting agencies must be told at the same threshold.
South Carolina.agency_name: South Carolina Department of Consumer Affairs, Consumer Protection Division
South Carolina.freeze_rights_note: You can place a free security freeze on your credit file with each of the three major credit bureaus, Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze blocks new accounts from being opened in your name until you lift it, and it is free to place, lift and remove under federal law.
South Carolina.notification_deadline_note: The statute sets no fixed number of days. Notice must be given in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay after discovery, allowing time for law enforcement needs and for steps to determine the scope and restore the system. Notice is only required when illegal use has occurred or is reasonably likely, or the use creates a material risk of harm.
South Carolina.private_right_note: An injured South Carolina resident may sue: damages for a willful and knowing violation, actual damages only for a negligent violation, plus an injunction and attorney's fees and court costs if successful.
South Carolina.state_note: South Carolina routes breach complaints through the Department of Consumer Affairs, which also sets the administrative fine for knowing and willful violations, rather than through the Attorney General, and it is one of the few states in this set where an injured consumer can sue directly under the breach law itself.
South Carolina.statute_name: Financial Identity Fraud and Identity Theft Protection Act
